A one square-metre slab of turf cost $8.50. If the area to be turfed is 12 m ×7.5 m, the total cost of the turf is____

Amal is building a square sandpit for his children to play in. He decided to make each of its sides 4 m long. He is going to put a boundary of pavers around the sandpit 400 mm wide.

If the pavers are 800 mm long and 400 mm wide, Amil will need _____
pavers.

Sandpit:4m = 4000mm

Paver width: 400mm

Paver width(Boundary width): 400 mm

Paver length: 800 mm

 Determine the dimensions of the outer square.

 The pavers go around the outside of the sandpit.

The boundary adds width to both sides of the sandpit (left and right, or top and bottom).
Outer side length = Sandpit side + 2 times Boundary width)
3. Calculate the area of the paver boundary You need the area of just the ring of pavers, not the whole square including the sandpit.

Calculate the area of the large outer square (Outer side times Outer side).
Calculate the area of the inner sandpit (4,000 mm times 4,000 mm).
Subtract the inner area from the outer area.

4. Calculate the area of a single paver

Area of one paver = Length times Width (800 text mm times 400 text mm.
5. Determine the number of pavers

Divide the total boundary area (from Step 3) by the area of a single paver (from Step 4).
Ensure the result is a whole number, as you cannot buy a fraction of a paver (though in this specific math problem, it likely divides evenly).

=22 pavers

notes.body:
SLOPE FROM EQUATION


y=mx+b

m=rise/run

x=x

b= when x=0 what does y=?

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

SYSTEM OF EQUATIONS

You are travelling in some type of fantasy land. And you're trying to get to the castle to save someone. But to get there, you have to cross a river. You can't swim across it because it's a very rough river. So you have to cross the bridge. And as you approach the bridge, a troll shows up. And he says, well, I'm a reasonable troll. You just have to pay $5. And when you look a bit more carefully, you see a sign that says $5 to cross the bridge. Now, unfortunately for you, you have no money in your pocket. And so the troll says, well, you can't cross. But you say, I need to really, really get to that castle. And so the troll says, well, I'll take some pity on you. Instead of paying the $5, I will give you a riddle: I am a rich troll because I get to charge everyone who crosses the bridge. And actually, I only accept $5 or $10 bills. Obviously, if you give me $10, I'll give you $5 back. I like to save my money. And I know, because I count my money daily, that I have a total of 900 $5 and $10 bills. And he (the troll) says, "Because I'm very sympathetic, I'll give you another piece of information." If you add up the value of all my money, which is all $5 and $10 bills that I have, it is $5500. Now you have 10 minutes to solve it, or he will do something horrible to you, like push you in the river. The riddle is:How many 5's and 10's do I(the troll)have?

Let f = the number of $5 bills.                           <-----system of equations
      t = the number of $10 bills.

f + t = 900

5f                 +                       10t   =    5500.    <-----also system of equation
^                                            ^
 l                                             l 
value of $5 bills          value of $10 bills 



To work out: draw a linear graph with f and t axes. There must be a 500 and 100 point on both the x and y (or t and f with respect), then consider the equations above with the opposite number = 0 (e.g. f=0, t=900) and then graph all four points. Then connect the lines and find the point where both lines intersect, and that is the answer.

So you would get 700 5-dollar notes and 200 10-dollar notes.
